directions.label: Practical Tips
directions.guidance: Give one concrete, immediately usable technique. The reader should be able to apply it today with any camera, including a phone. Always mention where or when to try it.

subjects.label: Natural lighting
subjects.guidance: Direction, quality and timing of natural light: window light, golden hour, open shade, overcast diffusion, and how light direction changes the mood of a portrait.

subjects.label: Composition and framing
subjects.guidance: Framing decisions: leading lines, foreground layers, symmetry, negative space, and choosing what to leave OUT of the frame.

subjects.label: Background selection
subjects.guidance: Controlling what sits behind the subject: clean backgrounds, colour clashes, distracting elements, and moving your feet instead of zooming.

subjects.label: Portrait distance and lens choice
subjects.guidance: How shooting distance changes facial perspective; why standing closer with a wider frame feels more intimate than zooming from far away.

subjects.label: Photographing events
subjects.guidance: Coverage thinking: arriving early, reading the room's key moments, working with available light, and backing up on site.

directions.label: Common Mistakes
directions.guidance: Name a real mistake beginners make, explain briefly why it hurts the image, and give the fix. Never shame the reader — everyone started there.

subjects.label: Missed focus
subjects.guidance: Focus point selection, eye-focus in portraits, shutter speed sufficiency, and why focusing and recomposing can shift the plane of focus.

subjects.label: Distracting backgrounds
subjects.guidance: Trees growing out of heads, bright corners stealing attention, clutter behind subjects — and the two-step fix of angle and aperture.

subjects.label: Flat exposure decisions
subjects.guidance: Trusting auto exposure on high-contrast scenes, losing highlights that cannot be recovered, and exposing for the subject instead of the scene.

subjects.label: Spray and pray
subjects.guidance: Burst-shooting through a moment instead of anticipating it; why slowing down produces better frames and a cleaner card.

directions.label: Mini Lessons
directions.guidance: Teach one concept properly in under 60 words: name it, explain the mechanism simply, show how to see it. Keep it technique-based, never historical or statistical.

subjects.label: The rule of thirds
subjects.guidance: What the grid actually does for balance, when to break it deliberately (centred symmetry, clean minimalism), and why it is a starting point, not a law.

subjects.label: Depth of field
subjects.guidance: How aperture, distance and focal length jointly control what is sharp; why background separation is more about distance than aperture alone.

subjects.label: Shutter speed
subjects.guidance: Freezing motion vs intentionally blurring it; how shutter speed is a creative decision about movement, not just a brightness setting.

subjects.label: Light and exposure
subjects.guidance: Exposure as a conversation between aperture, shutter and ISO; how seeing light as quantity changes the way you walk into a scene.

directions.label: For Your Business
directions.guidance: Connect photography craft to a business outcome a client cares about — product sales, brand trust, team image, event memory. Teach first; the value of hiring a professional should be implied, never pitched.

subjects.label: Product photography
subjects.guidance: How clean product images reduce buyer doubt: consistent backgrounds, honest colour, showing scale and detail.

subjects.label: Brand presentation
subjects.guidance: Why consistent visual treatment across photos builds recognition; how a business can define its own light, colour and mood standards.

subjects.label: Business portraits
subjects.guidance: What makes a professional portrait work: approachable expression, clean context, consistent crop; why team photos should look like one family.

subjects.label: Professional event coverage
subjects.guidance: The difference between snapshots and documentation: key-moment anticipation, stakeholder coverage lists, and delivery reliability.

directions.label: Let's Talk Photography
directions.guidance: Ask an inviting question about how people shoot or choose photos today. Keep it answerable in one sentence and friendly, never survey-like.

subjects.label: Favourite photos
subjects.guidance: Questions about which photos people keep coming back to and why memory attaches to certain frames.

subjects.label: Phone vs camera
subjects.guidance: The friendly debate: when the phone in the pocket is the right tool, and what a dedicated camera still does better.

subjects.label: Creative challenges
subjects.guidance: Small prompts readers can try this week — one subject, one light source, ten frames — framed as play, not homework.
